bullets.text: Home built out through the left side. Home 5 found Home 6 between Away's first and second lines with a pass rated Optimal, and Home 3 repeated the pattern into the left half-space.
When Away pressed with both forwards, Home's passes out of the back were more often rated Suboptimal or Poor. Two clear cases: a pass under high pressure that kept the ball, and one that was lost.
Away's pressing trigger was a pass back to Home 1. In the cited sequence Home 5 played back under high pressure with few forward options in the ring.
Home 8 received under high pressure while facing his own goal. This moment has lower tracking confidence, so treat the pressure reading with care.
In the second half Home lost the ball in midfield under high pressure, and Away's first action was a long carry through the centre.
Home 10 chose a square pass when a forward pass to a teammate in the ring had the higher value. The square pass kept possession, and the model rates it Suboptimal, not wrong.
Home 9 made an off-ball run into the channel that carried a high movement value, and the next pass from Home 6 went square instead. The run was not found.

limitations: Decision quality is a model estimate from tracked positions. It is not a ground-truth rating of a player.
Readings on frames below 0.75 confidence are marked and should be checked on the pitch before use.
No wearable data is connected, so this brief contains no physical load context.

bullets.text: Home progressed through the centre early in the match. Home 5 and Home 6 played forward into midfield, and both passes carry an event-only estimate rather than a measured rating.
A pass out from the back was lost after the feed tagged a pressure event. The feed records that pressure happened, not how close the opponent was.
A second-half loss in the middle third handed Away the next possession. With no off-ball positions in this feed, Ponta cannot show what Home's shape looked like at that moment.
Home 8 played a long pass to Home 9, more direct than the passes around it. Alternatives cannot be ranked without player positions.
Home 10 played wide to Home 11 late in the match. The event-only estimate for this pass spans more than one band, and should be read as a range.

limitations: This match has event data only. Decision quality is an estimate from start and end locations, shown as a range, and is not comparable with measured ratings from tracking data.
Opposition pressure, control zones and off-ball movement are Blocked for this match.
Event coordinates in the feed are rounded, so confidence is lower throughout.

bullets.text: Sprint efforts were spread across both periods rather than concentrated early. Home 7 and Home 11 each appear in the cited efforts.
Home 9 completed two sprint efforts close together in the second period. The cluster coincided with a rise in high-speed distance for that block, and is shown as context only.
One sprint effort has lower signal quality, so its peak speed should be read as approximate.
The last cited effort came late in the session. Load is described as context only: Ponta makes no medical, readiness or injury claims.
Home 11 repeated sprint efforts across the first period, with a longer gap before the second-half cluster.

limitations: This session has wearable data only. Opposition pressure, control zones, passes and carries are Blocked.
Physical context is shown as association with confidence bands. Nothing here predicts injury or fatigue.
Peak speeds come from unit samples at 10 Hz and carry measurement error.
